worked_solution:
By Newton’s second law,

$$
F(t)=ma(t),
$$

where $F(t)$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a(t)$ is the acceleration.

To find the velocity $v(t),$ we differentiate the displacement $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(t)) \\  & =\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[{({t}^{2}+1)}^{-1}] \\  & =-{({t}^{2}+1)}^{-2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+1) \\  & =-\frac{1}{{({t}^{2}+1)}^{2}}\cdot 2t \\  & =-\frac{2t}{{({t}^{2}+1)}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force, in Newtons, is

$$
\begin{aligned}F(t) & =ma(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot [-\frac{2t}{{({t}^{2}+1)}^{2}}] \\  & =-\frac{t}{{({t}^{2}+1)}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$
